gloss: to give off a pleasant fragrance; to be redolent

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {薫|かお}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to give off a pleasant fragrance; to be fragrant
definitions.explanation: To emit an agreeable scent or aroma. A more literary and elevated word than {香|かお}る, often used to evoke refined or atmospheric fragrance.

examples.japanese: {花|はな}が{薫|かお}る{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's the season when the flowers are fragrant.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}に{薫|かお}る{梅|うめ}の{香|か}りが{心地|ここち}よい。
examples.english: The plum blossom fragrance carried on the breeze is pleasant.

examples.japanese: {新緑|しんりょく}が{薫|かお}る{五月|ごがつ}の{朝|あさ}は、{散歩|さんぽ}するのに{最高|さいこう}だ。
examples.english: A May morning fragrant with fresh greenery is perfect for a walk.

notes:
A godan verb (る row) that is a literary variant of {香|かお}る. While both mean "to be fragrant," {薫|かお}る has a more refined, evocative quality. It is especially associated with classical poetry and seasonal writing.

WRITING:
The kanji {薫|かおる} suggests a warm, enveloping fragrance (related to smoking or incense), while {香|かおる} is the more general character for scent. In modern usage, {薫|かお}る tends to appear in literary or poetic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風|かぜ}{薫|かお}る{五月|ごがつ} — fragrant-breeze May (a classic seasonal expression)
- {緑|みどり}が{薫|かお}る — the greenery is fragrant
- {花|はな}が{薫|かお}る — the flowers are fragrant

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {香|かお}る — to be fragrant; the standard form, used more broadly in everyday contexts
- {匂|にお}う — to smell; neutral as to whether the scent is pleasant or unpleasant, while {薫|かお}る always implies a pleasant fragrance
